obtained.how: the agencies' own public map services, queried through the ArcGIS REST API on 2026-11-26. MDIFW's Wildlife Habitat Data MapServer on gis.maine.gov: layers 4 Deer Wintering Areas, 7 Inland Waterfowl and Wading Bird Habitat, 9 Significant Vernal Pools, 11 Endangered Threatened and Special Concern Wildlife. MDIFW's ArcGIS Online organization (services1.arcgis.com/RbMX0mRVOFNTdLzd): ConservationLands_EagleNests, EagleNestDistribution_5yearIntervals, BirdAtlas_BAEA_BlockCodes, BirdAtlas_GBHE_BlockCodes, MEIFW_BirdAtlasBlockCompletion, WinterAtlasResults, and the Maine Stream Habitat Viewer base layers (0 Crossings, 1 Dams, 9 Documented Habitat, 16 Non-Native Fish). Each response is saved as MDIFW_nd-2.<layer>.json; their attribute tables are dumped to MDIFW_nd-2.gis.txt and the service and layer definitions (copyright, renderer labels, field units) to MDIFW_nd-2.layers.txt

bibliography.checked_against: the services' own descriptions, copyright lines and ArcGIS Online item records, read 2026-11-26
bibliography.corrections: The entry bundles separate, undated, continuously updated services, and most are not at the one URL it gives. For the rewrite, list each layer with its URL and the access date (26 November 2026). (1) MDIFW Wildlife Habitat Data MapServer, https://gis.maine.gov/mapservices/rest/services/ifw/Wildlife_Habitat_Data/MapServer: layers 4 (Deer Wintering Areas), 7 (Inland Waterfowl and Wading Bird Habitat), 9 (Significant Vernal Pools) and 11 (Endangered Threatened and Special Concern Wildlife, 'updated daily'). (2) MDIFW eagle-nest services ConservationLands_EagleNests and EagleNestDistribution_5yearIntervals (data last edited 8 August 2019). (3) The 2nd Maine Bird Atlas (2018–2022) services BirdAtlas_BAEA_BlockCodes, BirdAtlas_GBHE_BlockCodes, MEIFW_BirdAtlasBlockCompletion and WinterAtlasResults. Groups 2 and 3 are at https://services1.arcgis.com/RbMX0mRVOFNTdLzd/ArcGIS/rest/services/, all copyright MDIFW. (4) The Maine Stream Habitat Viewer base layers, https://services1.arcgis.com/RbMX0mRVOFNTdLzd/ArcGIS/rest/services/Maine_Stream_Habitat_Viewer/FeatureServer (layers 0 Crossings, 1 Dams, 9 Documented Habitat, 16 Non-Native Fish; data last edited 16 November 2022). The Viewer is credited to 'Maine Department of Inland Fisheries & Wildife, US Fish and Wildlife Service', so cite it as MDIFW & USFWS. In the text, 'MDIFW GIS map services' should name the layer.
bibliography.quote: Base layers for the Maine Stream Habitat Viewer.

claims.claim: Route 169 crosses Hot Brook on a metal pipe-arch culvert 17 ft wide, 10 ft high and 86 ft long (5.2 × 3.0 × 26 m)
claims.source_value: Site 6796, Hot Brook at Route 169 ([coordinates withheld]): 'Pipe Arch/Elliptical Culvert', metal; inlet 17 ft wide and 10 ft high; outlet 17 ft wide and 9.9 ft high; 86 ft long
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), Maine Stream Habitat Viewer layer 0 Crossings, attribute table, Site_ID 6796
claims.quote: Inlet_Width: 17 | Inlet_Water_Depth: 1.5 | Inlet_Height: 10 | Crossing_Length: 86
claims.conditions: units ft (the layer's field aliases: 'Inlet Width (ft)', 'Crossing Length (ft)'); one culvert
claims.note: The metric conversions are right. The paper's 'about 2.5 km above the lake' is the project's NHD measurement, not the Viewer's.

claims.quote: Crossing_Class: Potential Barrier | Stream: Hot Brook | Road: Route 169

claims.claim: the state's non-native-fish layer marks both lakes as holding a confirmed non-native species, without naming it
claims.source_value: Upper Hot Brook Lake and Lower Hot Brook Lake polygons 'Confirmed: Y' (Region F); Hot Brook's three segments 'Confirmed: N'; the layer's only fields are name, region and Confirmed
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), Maine Stream Habitat Viewer layer 16 Non-Native Fish, attribute table
claims.quote: GNIS_Name: Upper Hot Brook Lake | Region: F | Confirmed: Y
claims.conditions: undated layer (data last edited 16 November 2022)

claims.claim: the state's alewife-habitat layer, of unstated date, still marks both lakes 'Inaccessible – not stocked'
claims.source_value: Upper (890.3 ac) and Lower (683.9 ac) both 'Inaccessible - not stocked' and 'No Commercial Harvest'; Hot Brook and the connecting brook mapped as 'Stream'
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), Maine Stream Habitat Viewer layer 9 Documented Habitat, attribute table
claims.quote: LAKENAME: Upper Hot Brook Lake | Status_new: Inaccessible - not stocked
claims.conditions: no compilation date in the service; its data were last edited 16 November 2022
claims.note: The layer is named 'Documented Habitat' and does not name its species. Its stocking and commercial-harvest statuses mark it as the river-herring (alewife) lake layer, so 'alewife-habitat layer' is a fair label. 'Of unstated date' is right; the rewrite could add 'as served since November 2022'.

claims.claim: MDIFW's records show eagles at the Upper nest in July 2018
claims.note: No MDIFW layer holds a 2018 record for nest 476A. The 5-year series includes 2018 (other nests have 2018 records) but has only 476A-2008 and 476A-2013, and both nest layers give 476A's 'year last nested' as 2013. The ETSC layers hold no eagle record. The project note's date, 2018-07-20, is presumably the Maine Bird Atlas breeding confirmation (via GBIF). Cite that record (MaineBirdAtlas_, checked by its own reader), not 'MDIFW's records'.

claims.source_value: block Stetson Mtn_NW, Bald_Eagle code 4 = 'Confirmed'. The block ([block bounds withheld]) holds the west half of Upper, including the [island withheld: nest site] nest. The other three lake blocks are 'NA' (No data)

claims.claim: at least four other eagle territories lie within about 20 km of the lakes (MDIFW GIS map services; Maine Bird Atlas)
claims.source_value: nest sites within 20 km of nest 476A: Crooked Brook Flowage, Danforth (085A–G and one unnumbered site, 6.5–9.3 km); Baskahegan Lake (729A at 12.8 km; 084A–D at 15.5–16.5 km); Mattawamkeag River / Mud Pond, Drew Plt (350A, 15.0 km); East Grand Lake, Five Islands (137A, C, D, 18.2 km); Jackson Brook Lake / Drake Lake (18.5 km); Mattawamkeag River, Haynesville (384A, 18.7 km); Spednik Lake (086A–C, 19.4–19.8 km)
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), ConservationLands_EagleNests layer 0, attribute table, nests within 45.42–45.80 N, 68.21–67.67 W
claims.quote: PK_NestSit: 729A | NestSiteNa: Baskahegan Lake, Whitehouse Point shoreline -- Brookton Township | YearLastNe: 2013
claims.conditions: historical nest sites (several last nested decades ago); distances by project arithmetic from the layer's coordinates
claims.note: Distances are straight-line from 476A ([coordinates withheld]), planar approximation. Sites last nested in 2013 or 2018 lie at Crooked Brook Flowage, Baskahegan Lake, Drew Plt, East Grand, Jackson Brook Lake, Haynesville and Spednik, so 'at least four' holds even counting only recent sites. The atlas also confirmed eagle breeding in block Brookton_NW, just east of the lake blocks.

claims.claim: MDIFW maps eight Inland Waterfowl and Wading Bird Habitat polygons around the lakes
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), Wildlife Habitat Data layer 7, attribute table and geometry
claims.quote: IWWH_ID: Iwwh203682 | RATING: M | NOTES: 2008 (IFW) Clipped upland buffer on lake shores
claims.conditions: polygons rated High (203684, UMO-6416) or Moderate (the rest), mapped 2002–2008 (IFW) and 2003 (UMO; UMO-6514 updated 2011)
claims.note: The count is the project's box query and depends on the box. Only Iwwh203682 touches a lake (Upper's south end). Within 1 km of either shore lie six polygons: 203682, UMO-6514, 110664, 203654, 204089, and 203679 on the inlet, which falls outside the box. Two of the box's eight lie 1.8–1.9 km off (203684 east of Upper, UMO-6416 west of Lower). Distances are measured to MDIFW's own lake polygons (Viewer layer 16).

claims.claim: the mapped waterfowl and wading-bird habitat around the lakes includes Upper's south end, Lower's north end and Hot Brook below Lower
claims.source_value: At Upper's south end, yes: Iwwh203682 touches it, and UMO-6514 and Iwwh203679 lie on the inlet. No polygon touches Lower or its outlet brook. Iwwh203654 lies 0.41 km east of Lower's north-east shore (0.70 km from the brook). Iwwh204089 lies 0.27 km east of Hot Brook below Lower and 0.89 km from the lake
claims.location: web page (ArcGIS REST query), Wildlife Habitat Data layer 7, attribute table and geometry (Iwwh203654, Iwwh204089, Iwwh203682)
claims.quote: IWWH_ID: Iwwh204089 | RATING: M | NOTES: 2008 (IFW)

notes: Every service answered openly (HTTP 200, public ArcGIS REST); nothing was refused. Most of the paper's site facts from 'MDIFW's records' and the state layers check against the live layers. Three corrections: (1) the 'eagles at the nest in July 2018' is not in any MDIFW layer and should be credited to the Maine Bird Atlas record; (2) the waterfowl and wading-bird polygons near Lower lie 0.3–0.4 km off its north end and outlet brook, not on them; (3) the second deer wintering area is 3.4 km away, not 'within about 3 km'. The listed-species layer (layer 11) says it is updated daily and that static copies should not be kept more than a year, so cite it with the access date. Its other records near the lakes: Black Tern (Endangered) at Crooked Brook Flowage, Danforth, 2010–2012, about 3.8 km east of Upper; and two generalised Special Concern 'RARE ANIMAL' polygons (ELCODE ARAAD02020, Danforth 2013-6-14 and Bancroft 2013-5-10) that overlap the lakes (the Danforth one both lakes, the Bancroft one Lower). These match the project note. The paper's §3.8.5 'wood turtle occurrence in the drainage is unconfirmed' is consistent with them, since the species is hidden. The Viewer's crossing records also flag 'Inland_Waterfowl_Wading_Bird_Ha: Yes' at the Route 169 culvert. The bear and moose harvest-by-town layers (MDIFW_nd-3) sit on the same MDIFW server. show.mjs matched every 'MDIFW n.d.' in §3.8 to this key. The claims above are the ones these services support, wherever they appear in the paper (§2.3, §2.5, §2.6, §2.8, §2.9, §3.1.2, §3.2.6, §3.5.1, §3.5.3, §3.8.1, §3.8.4). The §3.8 'MDIFW n.d., … page' citations belong to the other MDIFW_nd-* entries.
